newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Ethiopia appeals for $2 billion in foreign aid.
newsitem.headline: Ethiopia appeals for $2 billion in foreign aid.

text.p: Ethiopia appealed on Tuesday for $2 billion from foreign donors for a three-year development programme and for urgent relief of its $4.4 billion external debt.
Finance Minister Sufian Ahmed made the appeal at a three-day meeting of a Consultative Group of the donors in Addis Ababa.
He said although Ethiopia had made encouraging progress in the five years since the overthrow of Marxist dictator Mengistu Haile Mariam the country still needed foreign help.
He said Ethiopia needed $2 billion -- project financing of more than $1.3 billion and balance of payments support of not less than $600 million -- for the period up to and including 1999.
Sufian called for "the most generous debt relief" from all creditors on Ethiopia's $4.4 billion external debt. Servicing the debt consumes up to 47 percent of export earnings.
He said that Ethiopia was grateful for $1.1 billion pledged at a Consultative Group meeting in Paris in 1994 but that it still needed substantial support in the next three years.

He said average annual Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth from 1992 to last year was 7.6 percent with agriculture growing by about 14 percent, industry by nine percent and the service sector by 6.4 percent.
He said inflation, which stood at 21 percent in the 1991/92 financial year, fell as low as less than one percent in 1995/96.
Sufian said the government was vigorously following a policy of cutting its direct involvement in economic affairs and strengthening private sector involvement in Ethiopian business.
